children: ChatGPT maker is in preliminary talks with investors after raising USD 122 billion in March, while CEO Sam Altman has ruled out a 2026 IPO

OpenAI is in preliminary discussions with investors for a fresh funding round that could value the ChatGPT maker at about USD 1.2 trillion, the Financial Times reported on Tuesday. The talks come months after the company raised USD 122 billion at an USD 852 billion post-money valuation.

The potential financing would value OpenAI about 41 per cent higher than its March valuation. The discussions were initiated by investors and remain at an early stage, meaning the size and valuation of any eventual transaction could change. OpenAI declined to comment on the report, according to Reuters.

The funding discussions come as OpenAI's latest artificial intelligence products have helped accelerate its revenue growth. The FT reported that strong interest in GPT-5.6 and Astra has helped take OpenAI's annualised revenue to about USD 40 billion after a slower start to the year.

The company has also continued to require substantial capital to develop and train its AI systems. OpenAI spent about USD 34 billion on AI model training last year, according to the FT, highlighting the scale of investment required as it expands its models and computing infrastructure.

OpenAI's latest funding talks follow its March financing, which closed with USD 122 billion in committed capital at a post-money valuation of USD 852 billion. The company said the financing would support the next phase of its AI development and expansion.
The March financing was anchored by major commitments from Amazon, Nvidia and SoftBank. Amazon committed USD 50 billion, while Nvidia and SoftBank committed USD 30 billion each.

OpenAI's March financing represented a significant increase in private capital committed to the company. Its post-money valuation of USD 852 billion provides the benchmark against which the reported USD 1.2 trillion valuation for the potential new round would be measured.

The potential funding round comes as OpenAI's plans for a public listing move beyond 2026. The company confidentially filed for an IPO in June, but CEO Sam Altman said in a Fortune interview published on September 12 that OpenAI would not go public in 2026.
The decision leaves a potential 2027 listing or a later debut as possibilities rather than a formally announced timetable.

OpenAI's funding requirements reflect the cost of developing increasingly capable AI models and operating the computing infrastructure needed to serve them. The company has been expanding its AI products while pursuing additional computing capacity to support model training and deployment.

For OpenAI, any new private financing would come before an eventual public-market listing and would further increase the capital raised by the company. However, the reported USD 1.2 trillion valuation remains a subject of preliminary discussions rather than a completed transaction.
